newsitem.title: USA: U.S. probes takeover of California district - paper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. probes takeover of California district - paper.

text.p: The U.S. Justice Department is reviewing California's 1993 takeover of the Compton Unified school district to determine whether state officials jeopardized the voting rights of local residents, according to a published report on Wednesday.
The Los Angeles Times reported that officials from the Justice Department's civil rights division have requested copies of reports on the school district's academic and financial troubles.

The federal officials have also requested documents outlining the reasons why the state reduced the local school board to an advisory panel and installed a state-appointed administrator to run daily operations, the Times reported.
"We're gathering information to see what, if any, action we could take," Justice Department spokesman Myron Marlin told the newspaper.

California officials took over Compton Unified in 1993 because the district could not meet its payroll. The state legislature loaned the district $20 million with the condition the state Department of Education appoint an administrator.
